title: Accessible Media Gallery
description: Develop a responsive media gallery featuring video with captions, audio with transcript, custom controls, a modal, and full mobile/touch accessibility.
problemStatement:
## Project: Accessible Media Gallery

You are building a media gallery showcasing a short documentary video and a podcast episode, complete with accessible controls and interactive features.

### Core Features
1. **Video Player with Custom Controls**
   - A video element with a WebVTT captions file (you can create a simple VTT for a short clip or use a sample).
   - Custom controls: play/pause, mute, volume slider, seek bar, captions toggle, fullscreen.
   - All controls must be keyboard operable and properly labelled with `aria-label` and state (e.g., `aria-pressed` for toggle).
   - Seek bar and volume slider must be native `<input type="range">` with `aria-valuetext`.
   - Keyboard shortcuts: Space for play/pause, Left/Right arrow to seek ±5s, Up/Down for volume.
   - The video must have a visible **audio description** button (if available), otherwise provide a text description of visual content beside the video.

2. **Audio Podcast Section with Transcript**
   - An audio player (native `<audio>` element) but with custom controls similar to the video (play, seek, volume).
   - A collapsible transcript (using `<details>/<summary>`) that contains the full text of the podcast, with speaker identification and sound descriptions. The transcript must be accessible and keyboard operable.
   - A live region that announces the current playback time when the user seeks.

3. **Image Gallery with Modal**
   - A grid of thumbnails (images). Each thumbnail has appropriate `alt` text and is a `<button>` (or a link wrapping an image) that opens a larger version in a modal dialog.
   - The modal must:
     - Use the native `<dialog>` element or a div with `role="dialog"` and `aria-modal="true"`.
     - Trap focus, return focus to the triggering button on close.
     - Have an accessible name (`aria-labelledby` to an image title).
     - Allow navigation between images (previous/next) inside the modal using arrow keys and buttons.
     - Announce the current image (e.g., "Image 3 of 10") via a live region.
   - On mobile, the gallery must support swipe gestures for previous/next, while also providing buttons as an alternative.

4. **Responsive & Mobile Accessibility**
   - The page must work on screens from 320px to 1920px.
   - All touch targets (custom controls, thumbnails) must be at least 44×44 CSS pixels.
   - Avoid multi‑finger gestures without alternatives; provide tap/button alternatives for any swipe actions.
   - Test orientation: portrait and landscape both functional.

5. **Accessibility Testing**
   - The final app must pass axe DevTools with zero violations.
   - Manual keyboard test: all features operable without mouse, focus visible.
   - Screen reader test: with VoiceOver/NVDA, verify that controls announce properly, captions are toggled, modal traps focus, and dynamic updates (seek time, image slide number) are announced.

### Technical Constraints
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript (vanilla or with a lightweight helper).
- No heavy frameworks, but you may use small libraries for focus trapping if not native `<dialog>`.
- Provide a sample video and audio (or use free samples like Big Buck Bunny) and a sample VTT file with at least 3 captions.
- The transcript can be static text.

### Deliverable
A complete, working web application that is accessible across devices and assistive technologies.
requirements: Video player with custom accessible controls, captions, and audio description provision
Audio player with custom controls and collapsible transcript
Image gallery with accessible modal, focus trap, arrow key navigation, and swipe alternative
Responsive design with 44×44px touch targets and no orientation lock
All widgets keyboard and screen reader accessible (follow ARIA patterns)
Live regions for seeking announcement and modal slide counter
Passes axe audits and manual testing
hints: For the video player, use the native `<video>` element and hide its default controls; build your own controls that call `play()`, `pause()`, etc.
For captions, include a `<track>` element with a VTT file you create (even just a few lines for demonstration).
When implementing previous/next in the modal, update the `` src and alt, and announce the new slide number with a live region.
Use `pointerdown` and `pointerup` events for swipe detection, but also provide prev/next buttons.
For focus trapping in the modal, if not using `<dialog>`, query all focusable elements inside and wrap Tab/Shift+Tab.
Remember to test with a real screen reader; the seek announcement (current time) can be done with a `role="status"` live region that updates when the slider is changed.
expectedOutput: A polished, accessible media gallery app with all described features.
